# Strict-Typing Agent Team Registry

Live state of parallel agents working on the strict-typing plan
(`~/.claude/plans/stop-native-vs-tagged-tax.md`). One row per worker. Update
this file at every state transition (start of cluster, close of cluster,
blocked). The supervisor reviews this before dispatching new work.

## Why this exists

Two-or-more agents working in parallel on `bulldozer-strictly-typed` can
collide on shared territory (`type_schema/mod.rs`, `json_value.rs`,
marshal-layer files). Cluster-close merges already collided once on
`docs/defections.md`. This registry is the cheapest possible coordination
surface: agents declare intent up front; the supervisor catches overlap
before it's coded.

Surface root cause: `op_iter_done` / `op_iter_next` were dispatching every heap-bearing `iter_kind` through a single `slot.as_heap_value()` cast and matching the returned `HeapValue::*` variant. The cast is wrong-type recovery per the 5-arm soundness rule — slot bits are `Arc::into_raw(Arc<T>)` for the kind-specific `T`, not a `Box<HeapValue>` allocation. It worked coincidentally when the inner `T`'s discriminator at offset 0 happened to coincide with a `HeapValue::*` arm of the right shape. The killer case is `TypedArrayData::TypedObject` (post-bundle-A's `Arc<TypedBuffer<Arc<TypedObjectStorage>>>` carrier produced by `HashMap.entries()` / `Array.zip()` / `IteratorTransform::Enumerate`): `TypedArrayData::TypedObject` ordinal 20 aliases `HeapValue::Reference` ordinal 20, so `as_heap_value()` reads back as `HeapValue::Reference(_)`, surfacing "iter_kind=Ptr(TypedArray) but heap arm is Reference" at every `for entry in m.entries()`. **Fix**: rewrote both `op_iter_done` and `op_iter_next` to dispatch per-kind via `Arc::from_raw::<T>(bits)` + borrowed read + `Arc::into_raw(arc)` restore (the canonical receiver-recovery sound-pattern from `iterator_methods::clone_typed_array_arc` / `range_methods::clone_range_arc`). Each `NativeKind::Ptr(HeapKind::*)` arm now recovers the typed `T` directly: `TypedArrayData` for `Ptr(TypedArray)` (len from new centralized `typed_array_data_len` helper covering all 23 variants), `String` for `Ptr(String)` / `NativeKind::String`, `DataTable` for `Ptr(DataTable)`, `TableViewData` for `Ptr(TableView)`, `HashMapData` for `Ptr(HashMap)`. `op_iter_next`'s `TypedObject` element push (and the other 22 `TypedArrayData::*` arms) was already correct in the pre-existing `push_typed_array_element` helper — only the dispatcher needed the typed-Arc projection fix. **Smoke target end-to-end** under `--mode vm`: `m.set("a",1).set("b",2).set("c",3); for entry in m.entries() { print(entry.key, entry.value) }` → `a 1 / b 2 / c 3`. Pure-int array iteration (`for x in [1,2,3]`) and string iteration (`for c in "abc"`) still work (v2 raw-pointer fast path + Ptr(String) arm respectively). 3 new regression unit tests in `executor::loops::tests` pin the `TypedArrayData::TypedObject` carrier's done/next behavior so the wrong-type `as_heap_value()` cast can't creep back. **Out of territory**: `xs.zip(ys)` and `xs.enumerate()` smokes hit upstream surfaces — `handle_zip_v2` itself is `NotImplemented(SURFACE)` and `enumerate` isn't registered for v2 raw-pointer (`UInt64`-kinded) arrays; the global `builtin_zip` does construct the post-bundle-A Pair shape correctly but isn't reachable via the method-dispatch path for v2-carrier receivers. **Round 9 close report (8B.1 W12-jit-collection-arc-ffi-ctors-and-refcount, 2026-05-13)**:

Landed exactly the audit §10.2 / 8B.1 scope. 8 typed-Arc collection ctors + 16 per-HeapKind kinded retain/release entries + ownership.rs 8-arm dispatch extension. Round 9's surface is inert at the program-level smoke matrix (the EnumStore consumer + `jit_call_method` shell rebuild + cross-crate `VirtualMachine::jit_trampoline_call_method` API are Round 10 / 8B.2 territory) — verified Smoke 1 unchanged under `--mode jit`, Smoke 4 status unchanged (Round 6C/7B clean SURFACE preserved). Carrier-shape rule (audit §5) preserved: every body in `ffi/v2/collection_arc.rs` uses `Arc::into_raw(Arc<XData>) as u64` with `Arc::increment_strong_count::<XData>` / `Arc::decrement_strong_count::<XData>` at the matching kinded retain/release — Arc control block refcount at offset -16 per Rust Arc contract, NOT the W11 `UnifiedValue<T>` HeapHeader at offset 4. Mutex's `(bits, kind: u8)` carrier-pair correctly surface-and-stops on SENTINEL/unknown kind ord via the §2.7.7 #9 path (returns null bits + `SHAPE_JIT_DEBUG` diagnostic; the inner share is leaked rather than dropped with a fabricated Bool kind label — the principled response to a JIT-emit-time kind-source gap).

Tests: 26 new round-trip tests in `ffi/v2/collection_arc::tests` mirroring Round 7A's pattern at `ffi/result.rs::tests`. 8 ctor tests (refcount=1 verification, clean drop), 8 retain tests (1→2 transition + clean dual drop), 8 release tests (2→1 transition without dealloc + clean final drop), 1 null-bits safety pair (16 retain/release entries × bits=0 = no-op), 1 sentinel-kind surface test for Mutex.

Close gates (devenv exit-code-verified): `cargo check --workspace --lib --tests` EXIT=0 (full workspace, including shape-test); `cargo test -p shape-jit --lib` 361 passed / 0 failed / 26 ignored (baseline 335 + 26 new tests = 361 exact; no regressions); `bash scripts/verify-merge.sh` 12/12 Passed; `bash scripts/check-no-dynamic.sh` EXIT=0. Smoke 1 still passes under both VM and JIT (4950); Smoke 4 SURFACE state preserved unchanged.

Decisions called: Single combined module `collection_arc.rs` rather than separate `collection_ctors.rs` + `collection_arc_refcount.rs` files. Rationale: the carrier-shape rule from audit §5 is load-bearing AND bidirectional (ctors produce Arc-shape; retain/release operates on Arc-shape; mixing carrier shapes between them segfaults) — co-locating the ctor + retain/release for the same HeapKind family in one module makes the shared `Arc::into_raw` / `Arc::increment_strong_count` discipline visible at a glance, and keeps the audit §5 header comment as one source-of-truth rather than two. The audit §6 file table is non-binding on this point (it lists `collection_ctors.rs` + `collection_arc_refcount.rs` as separate-files candidates; the substantive constraint is the carrier-shape rule, which the single-module layout satisfies).

Surfaced items: None new. Round 9 closes exactly per the audit §10.2 / 8B.1 scope; no architectural gap surfaced. Round 10 (8B.2) inherits the dispatch from the EnumStore consumer for collection_ctor arm in `mir_compiler/statements.rs` and the `jit_call_method` shell rebuild — Round 9's FuncRefs are pre-resolved and ready for consumer-side wiring.

Of these, **~25 sites are construction sites** (`TypedArrayData::String(Arc::new(...))` / `TypedArrayData::Decimal(Arc::new(...))`) and **~120 sites are consumer match arms** that today receive `Ptr(HeapKind::TypedArray)` + `Arc<TypedArrayData::String|Decimal>` shape from those producers. The dispatch directive named the canonical producer sites (`object_creation.rs:518/799/544`, `concat.rs:240/255`, `heap_value.rs:3044` `build_specialized_from_heap_arcs`, `builtins/array_ops.rs:485` filled, `array_transform.rs:567/732/983/1460`); but the actual grep finds **additional producer sites the dispatch list missed**: `string_methods.rs:414/604` (`split` returning `Array<string>`), `array_ops.rs:262/304/467/676/696` (filtered/mapped/filled/empty/clone), `array_sort.rs:120` (sorted), `array_transform.rs:544/552/717/721/834/969/971/1093` (multiple derived ops), `array_basic.rs:259/324/425` (multiple). Migrating only the named root sites without the additional derived sites produces **partial mixed-carrier reality at runtime** — some producers push v2-raw `*mut TypedArray<*const StringObj/DecimalObj>` shape (under `NativeKind::UInt64` per the existing F64/I64/I32/Bool v2-raw convention at `v2_array_detect.rs`); other producers push legacy `Arc<TypedArrayData::String/Decimal>` shape (under `NativeKind::Ptr(HeapKind::TypedArray)`). This is exactly the parallel-implementation-defection-attractor pattern CLAUDE.md "Parallel-implementation across producer/consumer carrier-shape boundaries" refuses and that ADR-006 §2.7.24 Q25.A SUPERSEDED §4 #3 forbidden entry refuses ("Mixed-migration shape preserving some Q25.A specialized variants while migrating others to v2-raw `TypedArray<*const <X>Obj>` — the migration is single-target ... deviations require a separate ADR amendment"). **Additional architectural prerequisites surfaced**: (i) **No `NewTypedArrayString` / `NewTypedArrayDecimal` opcodes exist at HEAD** — the compiler at `crates/shape-vm/src/compiler/typed_emission.rs::TypedArrayKind` enumerates only `F64 / I64 / I32 / Bool`, and `should_use_typed_array` returns `None` for all other element types (including `ConcreteType::String` / `ConcreteType::Decimal`). For `Array<string>` and `Array<decimal>` literals the compiler emits the legacy `OpCode::NewArray` (which routes to `op_new_array` → `TypedArrayData::String/Decimal(Arc::new(TypedBuffer::from_vec(...)))`), NOT a v2-raw allocator opcode. Migrating the producer to v2-raw requires either (a) adding 8 new opcodes (`NewTypedArrayString`, `NewTypedArrayDecimal`, `TypedArrayGetString`, `TypedArrayGetDecimal`, `TypedArrayPushString`, `TypedArrayPushDecimal`, `TypedArraySetString`, `TypedArraySetDecimal`) + compiler emission via `TypedArrayKind::String` / `Decimal` variants + executor handlers + 4-table lockstep (`v2_handlers/array.rs` allocator handlers, `v2_handlers/v2_array_detect.rs` ElemType discriminants and read/write/push/pop dispatch arms), or (b) reworking `op_new_array`'s String/Decimal arms to push v2-raw shape (which breaks every existing consumer expecting `Ptr(HeapKind::TypedArray)` for that element type). Both routes have lockstep dependencies across the consumer side: `v2_array_detect.rs::V2TypedArrayView` + `read_element` / `write_element` / `push_element` / `pop_element` + `sum_elements` need `V2ElemType::String` / `V2ElemType::Decimal` variants AND the per-T retain/release plumbing at read time (each read of a `*const StringObj` element bumps the refcount before pushing the pointer onto the stack as `NativeKind::String` with `Arc<String>` bits — but the v2-raw element is NOT an `Arc<String>`, it's a `*const StringObj`; the cross-tier shape conversion at the array-element boundary needs ADR-level ratification because it's a new carrier-shape conversion not covered by existing ADR-006 §2.7.6 / Q8 dispatch tables). (ii) **The existing `Ptr(HeapKind::TypedArray)` consumer dispatch tables have ~30 sites across `printing.rs`, `arithmetic/mod.rs`, `comparison/mod.rs`, `typed_access.rs`, `objects/mod.rs`, `array_aggregation.rs`, `control_flow/mod.rs`, JIT layer** — each consumer assumes the slot bits are `Arc::into_raw(Arc<TypedArrayData>)` and reconstructs the Arc to dispatch. Adding v2-raw String/Decimal arms requires every consumer to discriminate between the two carrier shapes at the slot-bits layer, which is itself the §2.7.14 `UnifiedArray`-on-heap kind-byte pattern in a different framing if done via header.kind probe at the consumer (instead of via the producing-call-signature stamp that the typed-opcode approach uses). The clean disposition is to add separate typed opcodes (route (a) above) and let the compiler stamp the carrier shape via the producing opcode — but that's the multi-opcode-addition route gated on adding 8 opcodes + cascading compiler emission + 4-table lockstep + the cross-tier shape-conversion ADR. Migrating the producer to v2-raw requires either (a) adding 8 new opcodes (`NewTypedArrayString`, `NewTypedArrayDecimal`, `TypedArrayGetString`, `TypedArrayGetDecimal`, `TypedArrayPushString`, `TypedArrayPushDecimal`, `TypedArraySetString`, `TypedArraySetDecimal`) + compiler emission via `TypedArrayKind::String` / `Decimal` variants + executor handlers + 4-table lockstep (`v2_handlers/array.rs` allocator handlers, `v2_handlers/v2_array_detect.rs` ElemType discriminants and read/write/push/pop dispatch arms), or (b) reworking `op_new_array`'s String/Decimal arms to push v2-raw shape (which breaks every existing consumer expecting `Ptr(HeapKind::TypedArray)` for that element type). Both routes have lockstep dependencies across the consumer side: `v2_array_detect.rs::V2TypedArrayView` + `read_element` / `write_element` / `push_element` / `pop_element` + `sum_elements` need `V2ElemType::String` / `V2ElemType::Decimal` variants AND the per-T retain/release plumbing at read time (each read of a `*const StringObj` element bumps the refcount before pushing the pointer onto the stack as `NativeKind::String` with `Arc<String>` bits — but the v2-raw element is NOT an `Arc<String>`, it's a `*const StringObj`; the cross-tier shape conversion at the array-element boundary needs ADR-level ratification because it's a new carrier-shape conversion not covered by existing ADR-006 §2.7.6 / Q8 dispatch tables). (ii) **The existing `Ptr(HeapKind::TypedArray)` consumer dispatch tables have ~30 sites across `printing.rs`, `arithmetic/mod.rs`, `comparison/mod.rs`, `typed_access.rs`, `objects/mod.rs`, `array_aggregation.rs`, `control_flow/mod.rs`, JIT layer** — each consumer assumes the slot bits are `Arc::into_raw(Arc<TypedArrayData>)` and reconstructs the Arc to dispatch. Adding v2-raw String/Decimal arms requires every consumer to discriminate between the two carrier shapes at the slot-bits layer, which is itself the §2.7.14 `UnifiedArray`-on-heap kind-byte pattern in a different framing if done via header.kind probe at the consumer (instead of via the producing-call-signature stamp that the typed-opcode approach uses). The clean disposition is to add separate typed opcodes (route (a) above) and let the compiler stamp the carrier shape via the producing opcode — but that's the multi-opcode-addition route gated on adding 8 opcodes + cascading compiler emission + 4-table lockstep + the cross-tier shape-conversion ADR. (iii) **VM Decimal SIGSEGV at baseline** confirmed via baseline binary at `/home/dev/dev/shape-lang/shape/target/release/shape`: `let xs: Array<decimal> = [1.0d, 2.0d, 3.0d]; print(xs[0])` segfaults in VM mode (RC=139, "Segmentation fault (core dumped)") on baseline `3fe3ffa9` — independent of this sub-cluster's changes. The SIGSEGV is in the legacy `TypedArrayData::Decimal` consumer path (likely the v2-raw-heap aliasing class CLAUDE.md "v2-raw-heap aliasing class — 4 simulation tests deferred" describes). Migrating the producer to v2-raw with HeapElement retain/release at element-read time could either fix or worsen this depending on whether the consumer path's drop-glue accounts for v2-raw shape. Pre-existing SIGSEGV is owned as part of S2-prime-production's audit responsibility (per MEMORY.md "Don't blame pre-existing"); fixing it is non-trivial because it requires the full producer migration to land cleanly. **JIT String pre-existing W11-jit-new-array kind-source gap** also confirmed at baseline: `let xs: Array<string> = ["a","b","c"]; print(xs[0])` JIT-fails with "Route A surface-and-stop: SURFACE — Rvalue::Aggregate reached the kind-blind fallback ... ## Status values
| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|| `idle` | No active cluster; safe to dispatch new work. |
| `auditing` | Read-only Audit 1+2 in progress. No code edits. |
| `awaiting-decision` | Audit complete; supervisor must rule on architectural shape before migration starts. |
| `migrating` | Decision made; mechanical migration in progress. |
| `blocked` | Surface-and-stop fired (see `git stash list` on the worker branch). Needs supervisor ruling. |

## Update protocol

- **At cluster start:** the dispatching prompt (or the agent on first action) appends/edits its row with `active cluster`, `files owned`, status `auditing`. Supervisor confirms no overlap with other rows before greenlighting.
- **At decision-gate:** agent flips status to `awaiting-decision` after writing audit doc; surfaces to supervisor.
- **At cluster close:** agent flips status to `idle`, clears `active cluster`, updates "last update" date, and notes the close commit hash in the same row.
- **On stop-and-surface:** agent flips status to `blocked` and stashes the WIP. Supervisor triages stashes as part of session-start review.

## Forbidden zones (no edits without supervisor sign-off)

- `docs/defections.md` — append-only; new entries go at the end of file (see header comment).
- `docs/check-no-dynamic-baseline.txt` — only edit to **lower** a count after deletion progress. Never raise.
- `CLAUDE.md` "Forbidden Patterns" / "Renames to refuse on sight" — these lists are immutable to agents; only the supervisor adds entries (after a successful defection-attempt review).
- This file — agent rows are agent-editable; the schema/headers are not.

Lifecycle trace via eprintln instrumentation of `StringObj::new` / `::drop` / `::release_elem`, `HashMapData::insert` / `Clone::clone`, `read_keys_owned`, `build_filtered_kref::I64` reveals: filter's `data.insert(key.as_str(), v)` alloc returns the SAME ADDRESS as the `key.as_str()` data ptr — proving the `Arc<String>` for the key was freed BEFORE `build_filtered_kref` reads its `.as_str()`. **Producer/consumer chain identified**: `call_closure_with_nb_args_keepalive` at `crates/shape-vm/src/executor/call_convention.rs:737-739` (pre-fix) writes args bits to the new frame's stack via `stack_write_kinded` WITHOUT bumping the underlying refcount. The frame teardown at `op_return_value` → `truncate_stack(bp)` releases one share per arg via `drop_with_kind`; the caller's `args: &[KindedSlot]` carriers (constructed locally e.g. in `v2_filter` at `hashmap_methods.rs:1640`) ALSO own one share each and release on scope exit via `KindedSlot::Drop`. **Net: 2 releases per arg slot, 1 acquire** (the caller's original construction). The bytecode compiler at `crates/shape-vm/src/compiler/expressions/binary_ops.rs::emit_operator_trait_call` (5 call sites) + `unary_ops.rs` Neg/Not branches stamps `BytecodeProgram.operator_trait_dispatch_sites: HashMap<Span, (String, u16)>` whenever it emits `OpCode::CallMethod` for user-type operator overloading. Consequence: post-W8 the `ident` rule at `shape.pest:1476-1479` (which guards via `!(keyword ~ !(ASCII_ALPHANUMERIC | "_"))`) happily accepted `interface` as a user identifier; `interface CandleLike { timestamp: timestamp }` parsed as TWO statement-expressions: (1) `Identifier("interface")` + (2) `StructLiteral { type_name: CandleLike, fields: [(timestamp, Identifier(timestamp))] }`. Both `parse_program_helper` (`types.rs:15-32`) and the main `parse_program` (`mod.rs:57-105`) returned `Ok(items)` with 2 items each. | `phase-4b-round2-lang-2-continue-semantics` | `/home/dev/dev/shape-lang/shape-phase-4b-round2-lang-2-continue-semantics` | **CLOSED 2026-05-18 — v0.3 Phase 4b Round 2 sub-agent 2: W15.2-LANG-2 jit-continue-semantics fix.** Branched from `main` HEAD `b8ef6f75`. **Bug** (per `docs/cluster-audits/v0.3-w15-book-truth-reaudit.md` §6.2 — book snippet `A__fundamentals__control-flow__07__L0087` at `fundamentals/control-flow.mdx:87`): reproducer `for i in 0..10 { if i == 2 { continue } if i == 6 { break } print(i) }` produced VM `0\n1\n3\n4\n5` (correct) but JIT `0\n1` then infinite-loop timeout at 60s (the audit text "stops after first iteration past continue" was inferred from stdout flushing — empirically `timeout 60 ./target/release/shape run --mode jit ...` exits with code 124 (SIGTERM); the JIT prints `0\n1` then hangs forever at i=2). **Root cause**: MIR for-loop lowering at three sites (statement-form ForIn in `crates/shape-vm/src/mir/lowering/stmt.rs:602`, expr-form Range path in `crates/shape-vm/src/mir/lowering/expr.rs:1094`, expr-form generic-iterator path in `crates/shape-vm/src/mir/lowering/expr.rs:1307`) called `push_loop(after, header, ...)` — registering the **header** itself as the continue target. The post-body counter increment (`idx = idx + 1` in stmt.rs / generic-iter expr; `counter = counter + 1` in Range expr) was emitted as standalone statements AFTER the body but BEFORE the final `Goto(header)`. When the body fired `continue`, control jumped straight to `header` without ever running the increment → idx stayed at the value where `continue` fired → header cond still true → re-enter body → `continue` again → infinite loop. The bytecode-VM-side reference at `crates/shape-vm/src/compiler/loops.rs::end_range_counter_loop` (range-counter path) and `compile_for_loop` (generic-iterator path) correctly handle this by either patching `continue_jumps` to the increment block (range) or by emitting the increment BEFORE the body (generic-iterator). The MIR layer was missing the increment-block split. Note: the bytecode VM was never broken because it doesn't consume MIR — it uses its own bytecode emitter — which is why the bug only manifested under `--mode jit`. **Fix shape**: introduce a dedicated `continue_target` MIR block at each of the three sites. The block contains the increment statement and ends with `Goto(header)`. Body fall-through ends with `Goto(continue_target)`. `push_loop` registers `continue_target` (not `header`) as the loop's continue target. The body's `continue` statements terminate at `continue_target` so the increment runs exactly once per iteration whether the body falls through naturally or fires `continue`. Mirror of the bytecode-VM-side range-counter loop's `continue_jumps`-patched-to-increment pattern; preserves the C-style `for` MIR shape at `stmt.rs:653` which was already correct (continue → update_block → header). While-loop and loop-expr were also already correct (continue → header is correct for while because there is no separate update; continue → body_block is correct for loop). **Empirical verification**: audit reproducer `/tmp/continue-repro.shape` VM=`0\n1\n3\n4\n5` JIT=`0\n1\n3\n4\n5` (both EXIT=0 instead of 124 SIGTERM); function-wrapped variant `/tmp/cont-fn.shape` (`fn run() { for i in 0..10 { if i == 2 { continue } if i == 6 { break } sum = sum + i } sum }` printing `run()`) VM=`13` JIT=`13` (0+1+3+4+5 = 13); generic-iterator expression-form `/tmp/cont-generic.shape` (`fn run() { for x in [10,20,30,40,50] { if x == 30 { continue } if x == 50 { break } sum = sum + x } sum }`) VM=`70` JIT=`70` (10+20+40 = 70); generic-iterator statement-form `/tmp/cont-stmt.shape` (top-level for) VM=`70` JIT=`70`; while-loop with continue `/tmp/cont-while.shape` (sanity that while-loop continue → header is still correct) VM=`37` JIT=`37` (sum of 1..10 minus multiples-of-3 = 1+2+4+5+7+8+10 = 37). **Files changed (3 .rs + AGENTS.md row = 4)**: `crates/shape-vm/src/mir/lowering/stmt.rs` (+22/-3 — statement-form ForIn `continue_target` block + design comment citing W15.2-LANG-2 + bytecode-VM-side reference); `crates/shape-vm/src/mir/lowering/expr.rs` (+28/-3 across two arms — expr-form Range path + generic-iterator path, both with design comments cross-referencing stmt.rs ForIn arm); `crates/shape-vm/src/mir/lowering/mod.rs` (+88 — new regression test `test_for_range_continue_routes_through_increment_block` performing structural MIR inspection: locates the header block by its `BinaryOp::Lt`+`SwitchBool` shape, locates the increment block by its `BinaryOp::Add`+`Goto(header)` shape, asserts the body block (header's `SwitchBool::true_bb`) is NOT the same as the increment block, asserts the increment block is NOT the header itself — pins the invariant that distinguishes "broken pattern where continue=header" from "correct pattern with separate continue_target"); The bytecode VM dispatches `sqrt` via `OpCode::BuiltinCall(Sqrt)` per `crates/shape-vm/src/compiler/helpers.rs:4263::classify_builtin_function`, but MIR lowering at `crates/shape-vm/src/mir/lowering/expr.rs:2003` does NOT perform the equivalent producer-side classification — it leaks `MirConstant::Function("sqrt")` into MIR. When `MirConstant::Function(name)` matches a 1-arg math builtin name (`sqrt`/`abs`/`floor`/`ceil`/`round`/`sin`/`cos`/`tan`/`asin`/`acos`/`atan`/`exp`/`ln`) AND not in `function_indices`, dispatch directly to the typed-f64 FFI body (`jit_sqrt_f64` / `jit_abs_f64` / ... at `crates/shape-jit/src/ffi/v2_math.rs:232-294`). Empirically confirmed: any `[literal].method(...)` shape with a HOF (`map` / `filter` / `reduce`) hung; non-HOF method calls (`[1,2,3].len()` / `[1,2,3].sum()` / `[1,2,3,4,5]` literal-only) worked. **Root cause**: `crates/shape-vm/src/compiler/monomorphization/type_resolution.rs:1381` `concrete_type_for_expr`'s `Expr::Array` arm reads `compiler.array_element_types[span]`, but `compile_expr_array` at `crates/shape-vm/src/compiler/expressions/collections.rs:137` never populated that side-table for ANY array literal (only HashMap method dispatch sites at `compiler/{map_emission,v2_map_emission}.rs:867/882` etc. wrote into it). | `phase-4b-round5b2-bool-null-sentinel` | `/home/dev/dev/shape-lang/shape-r5b2-bool-null-sentinel` | **CLOSED 2026-05-19 — Phase 4b Round 5b-2 R5b2-bool-null-sentinel-cluster fix (v0.3-gating SOUNDNESS BUG class per supervisor ratify 2026-05-19; sister-class to LANG-9-spin-3-first VM/JIT divergence at R4-spin-3 close `28b79265`).** Branched from `main @ cebd03fa` (post-R5b-1 cross-cluster integration fix close). **Bug class**: 3 §2.7 carrier-semantics collision sites surfaced by W14.2-G6 e2e-features-functions triage (close `eb317757`) — all three share the COMMON ROOT CAUSE that pre-disposition the canonical null/unit sentinel was encoded as `(0u64, NativeKind::Bool)`, which collides at the bit level with legitimate `false` bool values (also encoded as bits=0 with `NativeKind::Bool`). The collision rendered the kind track unable to discriminate "null" from "false" — kind alone was decisive only when paired with bits, which violates the ADR-006 §2.7.7/Q9 parallel-kind-track-IS-the-discriminator invariant. **SURFACE-G6-BOOL-NULL** (VM-only divergence; JIT correct empirically): `is_null_kinded(0, NativeKind::Bool) == true` at `crates/shape-vm/src/executor/comparison/mod.rs:385` (pre-fix comment: "`(0u64, NativeKind::Bool)` is the §2.7 sentinel"). The bool-default-param fill-in path at `crates/shape-vm/src/compiler/functions.rs:1471-1493` emits `LoadLocal(val) + IsNull + JumpIfFalse + StoreLocal(default)` — when caller passes `false` for a bool-default param, the VM mis-detects "caller passed false" as "caller omitted; fill default" and returns the default instead. Pre-fix: `fn check(val: bool = true) -> bool { val }; check(false)` returned `true` under VM, `false` under JIT. **SURFACE-G6-LET-ONLY-BODY** (consumer-side at output adapter): the bytecode compiler's implicit-return path at `crates/shape-vm/src/compiler/functions.rs:1633` emits `PushNull + ReturnValue` for let-only fn bodies; pre-fix `PushNull` pushed `(0u64, NativeKind::Bool)` (executor/stack_ops/mod.rs:30) which materialized as `{"Bool": false}` in `slot_to_wire` at `crates/shape-runtime/src/wire_conversion.rs:75` (pre-fix arm: `NativeKind::Bool => WireValue::Bool(bits != 0)`). **SURFACE-G6-NONE-OUTPUT-ADAPTER** (consumer-side at output adapter): top-level `None` literal materialized as `{"Bool": false}` via the same `slot_to_wire` arm; `Constant::Null` and `Constant::Unit` in `op_push_const` at `executor/stack_ops/mod.rs:102-108` both pushed `(0u64, NativeKind::Bool)`. **DISPOSITION**: option (c) per dispatch recommendation — added `NativeKind::Null` as a non-parametric absence-of-value sentinel discriminator (mirror of `Bool` shape in Drop/Clone/wire/ABI tables — no Arc<T> payload, no refcount work). Per CLAUDE.md "Variants: `Float64` / `Int64` / `Int32` / `Int8` / `Bool` / `Unit` / `Null` / `Ptr(HeapKind)` / `String` / `StringV2` / `DecimalV2`" the `Null` variant was already documented as part of the enum vocabulary; this close brings the implementation in line with the documented enum surface (the variant did not previously exist in `crates/shape-value/src/native_kind.rs`). **Root cause** (per ADR-006 §2.7 carrier semantics + §2.7.5 producer-side stamp + §2.7.7/Q9 parallel-kind track): pre-disposition the `NativeKind::Bool` discriminator carried two unrelated semantic loads — "legitimate bool value with bits 0 or 1" AND "absence-of-value sentinel with bits=0". The same-name `let acc = acc` shadow tripped the MIR-side gap. **Discriminating empirical**: `let inner_acc = acc + item; ...` (different inner name) → VM=JIT byte-equal ✓; `let acc = acc + item; ...` (same-name shadow) → VM≠JIT, JIT loses fold state. At the struct literal `Box { value: 9 }`, `resolve_struct_runtime_type_name` (`compiler/expressions/collections.rs`) monomorphized the runtime type name to `Box<int>` and `compile_struct_literal` registered the specialized `Box<int>` schema by COPYING the base `Box` schema's fields VERBATIM (`collections.rs:998-1002`) — so the `Box<int>` schema carried `value: Object("T")`, the un-substituted type-parameter residue. Reading `b.value` emitted `MakeFieldRef { type_id: 20, field_idx: 0, field_type_tag: 6 }` (`FIELD_TAG_OBJECT`, via `field_type_to_tag` at `executor/typed_object_ops.rs:72`) — stamping a heap-pointer field tag on a slot that actually holds an inline `i64`. The subsequent `DerefLoad` → `read_ref_target` → `clone_with_kind(9, Ptr(HeapKind::TypedObject))` at `executor/vm_impl/stack.rs:116` dereferenced the raw scalar bits `9` as a `*const TypedObjectStorage` (`misaligned pointer dereference: address must be a multiple of 0x4 but is 0x9`). The JIT path produced the correct value (it reads the slot value directly by offset without the VM's kind-driven `clone_with_kind` retain). Additionally the pre-fix `all_defaults` early-`None` in `resolve_struct_runtime_type_name` (an optimization to skip registering a redundant `Box<int>` when every param resolves to its declared default) meant `Box<T = int>` + `Box { value: 9 }` resolved to the BARE `Box` schema (id 19) directly — also carrying `Object("T")` → same SIGSEGV. **(2) a SEPARATE, pre-existing, intermittent (~6%) TypedObject-reference double-free — NOT (d) scope, SURFACED named-and-cited**: `RefTarget::TypedField.receiver` is typed `Arc<TypedObjectStorage>` (`crates/shape-value/src/reference.rs:79`) but the runtime carrier is a v2-raw `HeapHeader`-at-offset-0 buffer allocated by `TypedObjectStorage::_new` (`Layout`-raw alloc, refcount in the embedded `HeapHeader`, NOT an `ArcInner`). `resolve_typed_object_receiver` (`executor/variables/mod.rs:2760`) runs `Arc::increment_strong_count::<TypedObjectStorage>` / `Arc::from_raw::<TypedObjectStorage>` against the wrong allocator layout (`Arc` expects the refcount at `ptr-16`; the v2-raw carrier has it at offset 0) → heap corruption that flakily manifests as `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`. **EMPIRICALLY PROVEN pre-existing and (d)-independent**: a fully NON-generic `type Box { value: int }; let b = Box { value: 9 }; print(b.value)` reproduces the double-free 9/150 (~6%) on UNMODIFIED baseline `6b6b50d8`; this is the same root-cause family as the phase-4 `op_get_field_typed` Arc-recovery fix (CLAUDE.md "Known Constraints" v2-raw-heap-audit) and properly belongs to a `RefTarget::TypedField` carrier-migration sub-cluster (change `receiver` from `Arc<TypedObjectStorage>` to the v2-raw `TypedObjectPtr` carrier — a VM-wide `shape-value` change touching every `MakeFieldRef`). The VM's i64 arithmetic handlers routed Add/Sub/Mul through f64 on overflow, silently corrupting any `int` arithmetic above 2^53. **Reproducer matrix at HEAD `71a88e4b` (release binary, canonical (ii) F' harness)**: `/tmp/intchk_b` (`2^53 + 1`) VM=9007199254740992 (WRONG — +1 lost to f64 rounding) / JIT=9007199254740993; `/tmp/intchk_c` (`2^62 + 2^62 + 1`) VM=4890909195324359000 (WRONG — f64 garbage) / JIT=-9223372036854775807; `/tmp/intchk_d` (`3037000500^2`) VM=9223372037000250000 (WRONG — f64-rounded) / JIT=-9223372036709301616 — JIT correct in every case (Cranelift `iadd`/`isub`/`imul` are pure two's-complement); compound-assign `+=`/`*=` (`/tmp/intchk_compound.shape`) hit the same bug (they desugar to the same `AddInt`/`MulInt` opcodes). **ROOT CAUSE (empirically bisected; opcode emission confirmed via `numeric_ops.rs:178` `TYPED_ARITH` table — plain `int`/`NumericType::Int` emits `AddInt`/`SubInt`/`MulInt`/`DivInt`/`ModInt`, all dispatched to `exec_typed_arithmetic`)**: `crates/shape-vm/src/executor/arithmetic/mod.rs` — the `binop_int_with_f64_overflow` helper (`mod.rs:244-259` pre-fix) and `PowInt` (`mod.rs:146-161` pre-fix) gated the i64 result against `fits_i48()` (an i48 inline range, `mod.rs:48`) and, on any value outside ±2^47 OR on `checked_*` returning `None`, fell through to `|a,b| a as f64 OP b as f64` → `NativeKind::Float64`. `fits_i48`'s own doc comment named it as a vestige of the deleted v1 `ValueWord` NaN-box i48-inline encoding ("Values outside this range would have been heap-boxed as BigInt under the v1 `ValueWord` encoding ... we promote to f64 instead, preserving the legacy overflow semantics"). The same f64-routing existed in `compact_int_checked_binop` (`mod.rs:443-463` pre-fix) on the i64 width path (`to_int_width()` returns `None` for I64 — `opcode_defs.rs:2196-2206`; that path is unreachable for plain `int` since the `*Typed` compact family only carries sub-64-bit `IntWidth` widths, but it was the same soundness violation in the same function family). The narrow VM widths (i8/i16/i32/u8/u16/u32/u64) were ALREADY correct — `compact_int_checked_binop`'s `to_int_width()==Some` path and the i32 `v2_handlers/int.rs` / `typed_handlers/int.rs` already used `wrapping_*`; the bug was 64-bit-specific. **FIX (`crates/shape-vm/src/executor/arithmetic/mod.rs`, ~70 LoC net production change)**: (i) `AddInt`/`SubInt`/`MulInt` now route through a NEW `binop_int_wrapping(op)` helper (replaces `binop_int_with_f64_overflow`) computing directly on i64 via `wrapping_add`/`wrapping_sub`/`wrapping_mul`, result kind unconditionally `NativeKind::Int64` — no f64 round-trip, no `checked_*`/`fits_i48` gate; (ii) `DivInt`/`ModInt` changed from plain `/`/`%` to `wrapping_div`/`wrapping_rem` so the single i64 division-overflow case `i64::MIN / -1` wraps to `i64::MIN` (and `i64::MIN % -1` to `0`) per ruling #3 instead of panicking — the div-by-zero `VMError::DivisionByZero` clean error is preserved; (iii) `PowInt` uses `wrapping_pow` for the non-negative-exponent path (no f64 promotion; negative-exponent f64 fallback retained — no i64 representation, never overflows); (iv) `compact_int_checked_binop` signature reduced to `(width, wrapping_op)` — the `checked`/`overflow_fallback` params and the f64-promotion arm removed, the i64-width path now wraps at 64 bits; (v) the vestigial `fits_i48` helper deleted (dead after the fix; it was a v1 `ValueWord` NaN-box artifact). **POST-FIX empirical matrix (release binary, canonical (ii) F' harness)**: `/tmp/intchk_b` VM=JIT=9007199254740993 ✓; `/tmp/intchk_c` VM=JIT=-9223372036854775807 ✓; `/tmp/intchk_d` VM=JIT=-9223372036709301616 ✓; compound-assign `+=`/`*=` VM=JIT byte-equal ✓ — all three reproducers VM byte-equal to JIT. **DIV/MOD edge-case investigation (per dispatch)**: the JIT (`compile_binop_int64` at `crates/shape-jit/src/mir_compiler/rvalues.rs:776-803`) lowers i64 Div/Mod as `trapnz(divisor==0, User(0))` + `sdiv`/`srem`. Empirically the JIT `User(0)` trap is an ILLEGAL INSTRUCTION — `/tmp/intdiv_zero.shape` (div-by-zero) and `/tmp/intdiv_min.shape` (`i64::MIN / -1`, Cranelift `sdiv` traps on division-overflow) BOTH SIGILL/core-dump under JIT (exit 132). The VM gives a clean `DivisionByZero` error and (post-fix) `i64::MIN / -1 = i64::MIN` defined wrapping. Under `--mode jit` the literal reached MIR with no proven kind → `compile_binop_dynamic_arith` SURFACE fallback. **ROOT CAUSE (empirically bisected; `/tmp/u64disc.shape` at HEAD VM lines 2+4 `false`, JIT `[jit-fallback] ... compile_binop_dynamic_arith: kind-untyped arith Div`)**: a bare int literal is `Literal::Int → NumericType::Int` (the default i64) — works for i64 context because `int` IS the default. Two producer-side kind-inference gaps: **(1) bytecode compiler** — `compiler/expressions/numeric_ops.rs::plan_coercion` mapped `IntWidth(W) + Int → NoCoercion(Int)` (widen to signed i64), so `a / 2` emitted the signed `DivInt`/`ModInt` (which discard operand kinds and always signed-divide, unlike the kind-aware `GtInt`/etc. comparisons). **(2) MIR lowering** — `lower_expr_to_operand` hoists every literal into a `Copy(Local)` temp whose slot kind is the width-blind `Int64`; the JIT's `uint64_binop_site` classifier only recognizes a DIRECT `Operand::Constant(MirConstant::Int(_))` sibling, so the hoisted-temp literal was never classified u64. **THE FIX (producer-side §2.7.5 stamp-at-compile-time, both halves)**: **(bytecode)** NEW `BytecodeCompiler::promote_int_literal_to_width_sibling` in `compiler/expressions/binary_ops.rs` — when one binary-op operand carries `NumericType::IntWidth(W)` and the other is a bare non-negative int literal classified `NumericType::Int`, promote the literal to `IntWidth(W)`; `plan_coercion(IntWidth(W), IntWidth(W)) → NoCoercion(IntWidth(W))` → emits `DivTyped`/`ModTyped`/`AddTyped`/... with the matching `NumericWidth` (the u64 path does unsigned `compact_int_divmod_u64`; the narrow widths truncate). Negative literals do not adopt unsigned widths. Width-GENERAL (covers `u64` AND the narrow `i8`/.../`u32` widths — VERIFY-BINDING #6 found narrow-`var OP literal` arithmetic was also broken in the VM and folded the same fix). Wired into both the `BinaryOp::Add` arm and the generic `Sub`/`Mul`/`Div`/`Mod`/comparison arm. **(MIR)** NEW `expr_is_u64_typed` + `lower_int_literal_as_direct_constant` in `mir/lowering/expr.rs` — in the `Expr::BinaryOp` arm, when one operand is a `u64`-typed expression (`u64` identifier, `Literal::UInt`, or a recursively-`u64` arithmetic sub-expression so `(a/2) == 5` resolves) and the OTHER is a bare int literal, lower the literal directly as `Operand::Constant` instead of hoisting it — the JIT's `uint64_binop_site` then sees the `(UInt64, Int64-literal)` pair and routes to `compile_binop_uint64` (`udiv`/`urem`/`Unsigned*`). MIR half SCOPED TO `u64` — the narrow-width JIT path (`compile_binop_narrow_int`, checkpoint-(c) territory) has a latent codegen bug that a generalized direct-constant lowering would un-mask; narrow programs keep the pre-fix MIR shape (literal hoisted → narrow JIT path declines → whole-function interpreter fallback → runs the now-fixed bytecode → VM==JIT preserved). NEW `MirBuilder::lookup_local_declared_scalar_type` getter. **Before/after VM==JIT (release binary)**: `/tmp/u64disc.shape` all 4 `print` lines `false`/fallback→`true` VM==JIT, JIT no longer emits the `kind-untyped arith ... SURFACE` fallback (0 fallbacks); `u64::MAX / 2` →9223372036854775807, `% 10`→5, `+1`→0 (wrap), `-1`→u64::MAX-1, `m*2`→0 (wrap), `100/a`→0, comparisons `a>100`/`a<100` correct; narrow `i8`/`i16`/`i32`/`u8`/`u16`/`u32` `var OP literal` arithmetic VM==JIT (`/tmp/nv.shape` 7/7). **VERIFY-BINDING (#6) per-width empirical result**: `u64_var OP literal` — BROKEN at HEAD, fixed (VM+JIT). `i8`/`i16`/`i32`/`u8`/`u16`/`u32 var OP literal` — VM arithmetic BROKEN at HEAD (literal widened to signed i64, narrow overflow failed to truncate/wrap), folded into the bytecode-compiler fix → now correct VM==JIT; the narrow-width JIT codegen path remains checkpoint-(c) territory and continues to fall back to the interpreter for hoisted-literal operands (no behavior change, no regression). **Gates (devenv exit-code-verified)**: `just check-clean` EXIT=0; Critically the comparison EXTENDS rather than truncates: an out-of-narrow-range literal/`int` (`let c:i8=44; c==300` — VM `44 != 300` false) keeps its real value, where the pre-fix arithmetic-style `ireduce`-to-narrow would have masked `300`→`44` and wrongly reported `true`. The `<K>` type-param does NOT make the monomorphization self-call guard fire for an `extend Vec<T>` method; `extend Vec<T>` methods intercept array dispatch regardless. **THE FIX (real pure-Shape implementation, in `vec.shape`)**: replaced the self-recursive body with a real pure-Shape grouping that returns a FLAT `Vec<T>` in which every element sharing a key is contiguous, groups in first-seen key order — for `[1,2,3,4,5,6].groupBy(|x| x%2)` the result is `[1,3,5,2,4,6]` (odds then evens). Single result array; for each position the method scans every earlier element to detect a first-occurrence key, then on a first occurrence scans the rest once and appends every matching element. All loops bounded by `self.len()` — terminating, never calls `self.groupBy`. **WHY FLAT `Vec<T>` NOT `Vec<Vec<T>>` BUCKETS OR `HashMap<K,Vec<T>>` — V3-S5 ckpt-5 COUPLING (the ε-2 honest finding, confirmed)**: a collection-of-collections return value CANNOT be constructed today — even a nested array literal `[[1,2],[3,4]]` or `[a,b]` of two array variables hits `op_new_typed_array(2)`/`op_new_array(2)` SURFACE (V3-S5 ckpt-5 consumer-cascade — the W12 typed-array-data deletion has not yet landed its construction-site rebuild, lands at ckpt-6); and the value's mere existence at user scope triggers `op_new_array(0)` at scope-exit drop. `HashMap<K,Vec<T>>` is equally blocked: HashMap keys MUST be strings (`m.set(0,...)` → `HashMap key must be a string (got kind Int64)`) so `int` keys are impossible, AND HashMap values reject array payloads (`HashMap.set(): value kind Ptr(TypedArray) incompatible`). The Rust PHF handler `array_transform::handle_group_by_v2` is itself a `ckpt2_surface` stub (REFUSED ON SIGHT to un-defer per task constraint). (b) the deeper fix (rewire MIR lowering at `stmt.rs:269-273` to NOT prefer_move for still-live `let`-source bindings, OR redefine `OwnershipModifier::Inferred` semantics) touches documented language semantics; v0.4 territory.
